stage: exploration; all source sequences previously viewed
question: Does a small load-conditioned state-space predictor improve next observed section3 width over persistence and load secant?
scope: same14 observations, three beams, section3 only, one-step rolling assimilation, no masks/images changed or neural training
primary: equal-weight mean of per-beam MAE on forecasts with >=2 historical observations (8 total)

target: next bias-contaminated mask-derived width; not independent true aperture or physical lifetime
state: [expected mask width, local slope per10kN]; initial state[first observed width,0], initial covariance diag[measurement variance,1]
measurement: H=[1,0], independent working Gaussian epsilon with R=sigma^2; forecast bands include next-observation R
assumption_rationale: fixed engineering scales in strip pixels, not estimated variance or correction; span plausible boundary perturbations without claiming calibration
no_selection: nominal settings fixed before execution; all9 noise scenarios retained, no best-setting promotion
intervals: Gaussian95% working predictive bands conditional on assumptions; 8 outcomes cannot establish calibration
comparison: candidate vs strongest simpler method, report mixed/negative beam results; no frozen previous result changed
resource_cap: local CPU NumPy2x2 algebra and plots, <1min; one nominal comparison plus fixed9 noise and perturbation scenarios
stop: after requested exports and plots, no architecture search, new inference or training
